target.name: ribonucleoside triphosphate catabolic process
target.description: Ribonucleoside triphosphate catabolism strips phosphates from ATP, GTP and related nucleotides, and it serves two quite different purposes: clearing extracellular nucleotides that act as signals, and cleansing the intracellular nucleotide pool of species that would corrupt nucleic acid synthesis. The ectonucleotidases here are membrane-anchored enzymes that hydrolyse nucleoside triphosphates and diphosphates on the cell surface or in the secretory and lysosomal system, terminating purinergic receptor signalling and setting the balance of ATP against adenosine that shapes platelet activation, vascular tone and immune responses.

target.name: phospholipase C-activating G protein-coupled acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway
target.description: Phospholipase C-activating G protein-coupled acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway is the excitatory arm of muscarinic cholinergic transmission, in which acetylcholine acting through Gq-coupled receptors mobilises intracellular calcium rather than altering cyclic AMP. It drives smooth muscle contraction in airway, gut and bladder, glandular secretion, and slow depolarising responses in neurons that support learning and memory; blocking it is the basis of bronchodilator and antispasmodic anticholinergic drugs.

target.name: negative regulation of protein catabolic process in the vacuole
target.description: Proteins delivered to the lysosome are usually destined for destruction, and this pathway covers the braking mechanisms that spare them, damping the rate and extent of vacuolar protein catabolism. The effect is largely a matter of sorting: cargo diverted away from the degradative lumen is recycled to the cell surface or the Golgi instead, so receptor levels, signalling output and membrane protein lifespan all depend on how strongly this restraint operates.

target.description: Water balance depends on vasopressin, a nine-residue hormone cleaved from the AVP precursor in hypothalamic neurons and released from the posterior pituitary when plasma osmolarity rises or blood volume falls. Acting through its receptors, it drives aquaporin-2 trafficking to the apical membrane of kidney collecting duct cells so that water is reabsorbed rather than lost in urine, and it also raises vascular tone and stimulates pituitary ACTH release through the AVPR1A and AVPR1B subtypes.

target.description: Learned vocalization is the capacity to acquire and refine vocal output by imitation and auditory feedback rather than producing it innately, the basis of human speech acquisition and of song learning in songbirds. It depends on cortico-striatal and cortico-cerebellar circuits that link auditory perception to motor sequencing of the larynx and articulators, and on the synaptic plasticity that lets those circuits be tuned during a sensitive developmental period.
